title: 1.1 Evaluating Algebraic Expressions

icans: I can evaluate expressions with one variable.
I can evaluate expressions with two or more variables using the order of operations.
I can write and evaluate expressions for real-life situations.

vocab: a __________ that stands for a number
an expression with numbers, variables, and _____________
_____________ numbers for the variables and simplify
grouping symbols, ____________, multiply and divide (left to right), add and subtract (left to right)

blocks.p: Evaluate each expression when x = 3 and y = −2. Take turns: one partner does a step, the other checks it and does the next.

blocks.sec: Part 2 · Notes and examples (fill in each note, then work the example)

notes: Order of operations: Order of operations: _______________, _______________, multiply and _______________ (left to right), add and _______________ (left to right).
Evaluating: To evaluate, _______________ each variable with its value, using _______________ around negatives.

blocks.stem:
Evaluate each expression.
a.  5x − 8 when x = 4        b.  2x² + 1 when x = −3
Evaluate a² − 3b when a = 4 and b = −2.
Evaluate (x + y)/z − 2y when x = 7, y = 5, and z = 3.
A phone plan costs $25 a month plus $0.10 per text. The cost is C = 25 + 0.1t, where t is the number of texts. Find the cost for 140 texts.
Evaluate 4m − n² when m = 3 and n = −5.

tickets.stem: Evaluate ab + c when a = 2, b = −3, and c = 10.
